title: GP7200 on A380 - measured spec for 1:1 modelling
frame: engine axis; station s = 0 at the spinner tip, positive aft; r = distance from the axis; top/bottom are the vertical meridian, inboard/outboard the horizontal

station_zero.source: TCDS IM.E.026 + p.106: spinner tip to fan case front flange 0.213 m (4.93 - 4.72 m dims). The split is put 0.05 m aft of that flange: photo Airbus_Lagardere_-_GP7200_engine_MSN111_(1).JPG shows the inlet outer barrel ending at the fan case front; the Trent analogue (FBW Trent mesh + p.111/p.112) gives +0.19 m; the TEC aft flange (4.92) then sits at the fan nozzle exit, inside the drawn core cowl; the red fan-plane line on the cowl lands at s ~0.41, just behind the fan case front. Uncertainty +-0.12 m on the whole nacelle relative to the engine.

key_stations.source: Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine: outline read from the PDF vector path; stations piecewise-linear between the printed dims (nose cowl 1.5 top / 1.17 bottom, fan cowl 2.18, thrust reverser 2.52, fan nozzle to plug tip 2.11); anchors (x pt, s m) [(167.92, -1.24), (178.9, -0.91), (219.3, 0.26), (293.1, 2.44), (378.9, 4.96), (448.5, 7.07)]
key_stations.red_line_source: photos ILA_2010_-_gravitat-OFF_-_Airbus_380_079.jpg (E1 and E2, 0.11-0.15 m aft of the split at 163 and 148 px/m) and Airbus_A380_(F-WWDD)_..._(248-28).jpg (~0.2 m)
key_stations.inlet_scarf: top highlight 0.33 m ahead of bottom (6.1 deg)

outer_nacelle.source: Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine: outline read from the PDF vector path; stations piecewise-linear between the printed dims (nose cowl 1.5 top / 1.17 bottom, fan cowl 2.18, thrust reverser 2.52, fan nozzle to plug tip 2.11); anchors (x pt, s m) [(167.92, -1.24), (178.9, -0.91), (219.3, 0.26), (293.1, 2.44), (378.9, 4.96), (448.5, 7.07)]; Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine: radius = (axis y 249.13 pt - y) / 33.37 pt/m; radial scale set so the side-view height (126.8 pt) equals the 3.8 m front-view width (front view on p.108 is a circle 121 x 121 pt; the 3.9 m height on p.107 includes the small pylon-junction bump); axis = plug tip and core-nozzle centres (y 249.12-249.17 pt)
outer_nacelle.symmetry: not axisymmetric: keel further from the axis than the crown (inlet and max section drooped below the axis), plan view assumed symmetric

inboard_outboard_estimate.source: estimate: no plan-view drawing; front views on p.107/p.108 are circular (3.8 m), so each section is taken as a circle through the measured crown and keel

max_section.source: Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine: radius = (axis y 249.13 pt - y) / 33.37 pt/m; radial scale set so the side-view height (126.8 pt) equals the 3.8 m front-view width (front view on p.108 is a circle 121 x 121 pt; the 3.9 m height on p.107 includes the small pylon-junction bump); axis = plug tip and core-nozzle centres (y 249.12-249.17 pt); width 3.8 m and height 3.9 m are the printed p.107 front-view dims

outer_nacelle.chines_strakes: none on any of the four nacelles (photos ILA_2010_-_gravitat-OFF_-_Airbus_380_079.jpg, Airbus_A380_03_(4825832887).jpg, A380_ENGINE.jpg, F-WWDD 248-27/28); none on the p.107 drawing

upper_aft_fairing.note: the top of the nozzle overhangs aft to s 5.22 (pylon/hinge-beam fairing, p.107 outline; visible in the ILA 079 photo)

highlight.source: Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine, lip front line of the outline

inlet.throat_source: estimate from photo Air_France_Airbus_A380-861_F-HPJA_@_Paris_CDG.jpg: dark throat circle 412 px / nacelle width 547 px x 3.8 m, corrected ~3% for depth -> 1.39-1.43
inlet.lip_outer_metal_band: polished lip skin from the highlight to the joint line 0.20 m (top) / 0.23 m (bottom) aft (p.107 line parallel to the lip; rivet rows visible in A380_ENGINE.jpg)
inlet.acoustic_liner: perforated liner from just inside the lip to the fan case (A380_ENGINE.jpg, F-WWDD 248-27)
inlet.abradable_rub_ring: pale olive ring ahead of and around the fan tips (A380_ENGINE.jpg, F-WWDD 248-27)

nose_cowl_fan_cowl_split.source: Airbus A380 AC (ac_a380_1223.pdf) PDF p.107, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-004-A01 Nacelle Dimensions - GP 7200 Engine (1.5/1.17 m)

panels.upper_longitudinal_line: line ~0.08-0.10 m below the crown along fan cowl and TR (p.107), the pylon/hinge interface edge

oil_tank_access_door.side: engine left side (seen on the outboard faces of E1/E2)
oil_tank_access_door.source: p.107 square + photo ILA 079 (labelled OIL TANK ACCESS DOOR)

tr_actuator_fittings.source: p.107 three rounded rectangles; photo ILA 079 E2 at 1.06 m aft of the TR front (drawing 1.07)

plug.shape: straight cone, half-angle ~19-21 deg, blunt tip; a ring of small vent holes/slots just aft of the nozzle exit (p.107, Lagardere MSN108 photos)
plug.photo_check: ILA 079 E1: plug 1.04 m long, base dia 0.77 m at 163 px/m (drawing 1.15 / 0.87; photo foreshortened)

spinner.fit: r = 0.675 * s^0.47 (rms 0.8 mm on the drawn part s 0-0.213); extrapolated: s 0.3: r 0.383, s 0.4: r 0.439, s 0.45: r 0.464
spinner.source: p.106 FIGURE-2-12-0-991-003-A01 silhouette (spinner visible ahead of the fan case, 62.96 pt/m); beyond s 0.213 estimate
spinner.colour: #1C1D1C matte black/charcoal with one white radial dash near the nose (A380_ENGINE.jpg, F-WWDD 248-27, Lagardere MSN111)

fan.le_source: estimate: red fan-plane line on the cowl (s 0.38-0.47) and fan case front flange at 0.213
fan.chord_source: estimate: wide-chord blades overlap strongly in A380_ENGINE.jpg; tip pitch 0.386 m x solidity 1.3-1.5; root pitch 0.123 m x solidity ~2.8
fan.sweep: swept tip, LE leaning aft ~10-20 deg over the outer third (estimate from Lagardere MSN111 photo)
fan.twist: stagger ~20 deg (root) to ~60 deg (tip) from the axis, ~40 deg twist (estimate)
fan.colour: #7E8082 bare titanium, darker in shade (#3C3427 measured inside the inlet in A380_ENGINE.jpg)

ogv.source: photo GP7000_MTU-Museum_20231112_03w.jpg: vane pitch at 9 o'clock gives 7.1-8.1 deg (44-51 vanes); station between the p.106 flanges at 1.50 and 1.86 (estimate)

thrust_reversers.source: AC 2-12-0 text p.104: reversers only on the inboard engines; outboard engines have fan exhaust cowls
thrust_reversers.type: fixed cascade, translating cowl, blocker doors; two C-duct halves hinged on the pylon
thrust_reversers.outboard_difference: same outer lines and the same 2.52 m length (photo ILA 079 E1 vs E2 and identical p.109/p.110 opening data), but no translating sleeve, no actuator fittings at s 3.4-3.6, no sleeve joint at 4.18; plain fan exhaust cowl halves latched at the bottom

engine_positions.obj_frame: X-Plane OBJ: x lateral (+right), y up, z aft (m); fuselage nose tip at z -35.19 (a380_exterior_009)
engine_positions.trust: lateral: mesh (x +-14.875 / +-25.757) agrees with AC p.32 span dims 29.6 / 51.4 m within 0.08 m. Vertical: AC front views give GP keel clearance +0.13 m (inboard) / -0.05 m (outboard) relative to the Trent; applied to the Trent mesh with the axis-to-keel difference. Longitudinal: AC plan view (p.33) puts the nacelle fronts at 22.23 / 29.94 m from the nose = z -12.96 / -5.25; the Trent mesh has -12.85 / -4.82, so the outboard mesh engine is 0.43 m further aft than the drawing (open question); recommendation keeps the mesh pylons (fan-cowl split at the Trent's).

recommended.how: x from the installed mesh fan disc (AC p.32 gives +-25.7 m, mesh within 0.08 m); y = Trent mesh axis -0.515 + AC keel-clearance change -0.05 m (p.107 GP vs p.112 Trent) + (GP drawing axis-to-keel 1.972 - Trent mesh axis-to-keel 2.075); z puts the GP nose-cowl/fan-cowl split where the Trent's is (Trent mesh top lip -4.817 + 1.63 m, p.112), both fan cowls being 2.18 m long; toe/pitch kept from the mesh (no Airbus figure for installation angles)

flowpath.source: estimate: no GP7200 cross-section in the local refs; radii placed inside the measured casing envelope with typical hub/tip ratios; exit tied to the measured core nozzle (p.107)

estimate: between fan hub 0.47 and OGV hub ~0.85
estimate: booster inside the OGV / fan-frame region (OGV row s 1.50-1.86)
estimate: transition duct through the fan hub frame struts
estimate: casing r 0.414-0.424 at s 2.38 (p.106) minus ~0.045 case and tip allowance; hub/tip 0.65
estimate: casing r 0.42-0.44 (p.106); hub/tip ~0.9 at exit
estimate: TCF flange r 0.59 (p.106); flowpath ramps outward through the TCF

fan_hub_and_splitter.fan_hub_source: estimate: spinner fit r = 0.675 s^0.47 (p.106) extrapolated to s ~0.45; photo A380_ENGINE.jpg spinner/fan proportion ~0.5 m
fan_hub_and_splitter.ogv_hub_source: estimate: MTU photo GP7000_MTU-Museum_20231112_03w.jpg inner/outer OGV ring ratio 0.53 x OGV tip ~1.50 = 0.79; drawing p.106 fan hub frame ring r 0.87-0.91 at s 2.27-2.33; take 0.85

lpc_booster.station_source: estimate: p.106 gives only the whole LP compressor module (fan + booster) s 0 to 2.33; booster placed under the OGV region
lpc_booster.counts_note: not found in the local refs; modelling estimate only (typical PW4000-112 / GE90-class boosters): rotors ~70-90 blades, stators ~90-120 vanes per row, plus an inlet guide vane row

intermediate_case_fan_hub_frame.station_source: drawing p.106: OGV casing aft flange 1.861 to HPC front flange 2.328
intermediate_case_fan_hub_frame.struts_note: not visible in any ref; estimate 8 struts, the 6 o'clock one carrying the radial drive shaft (p.106 dash-dot line at s 2.65). The OGV row has 2 thick structural struts at 12 and 6 o'clock (MTU photo 03w)

hpc.station_source: Airbus A380 AC PDF p.106, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-003-A01 Engine Dimensions - GP7200 (vector paths, 62.96 pt/m from the 4.93 m and 4.72 m dims, 0.1% apart), HP COMPRESSOR dimension
hpc.variable_stators: estimate: IGV + first 4-5 stator rows variable; p.106 shows ~5 ring/lever features on the forward HPC case s 2.38-2.62 (VSV unison rings) and the core is GE90-derived
hpc.counts_note: not found; modelling estimate 50-80 blades per rotor

diffuser_combustor.type: single annular combustor (estimate, GE90-derived core; drawing only says COMBUSTOR SECTION)
diffuser_combustor.station_source: Airbus A380 AC PDF p.106, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-003-A01 Engine Dimensions - GP7200 (vector paths, 62.96 pt/m from the 4.93 m and 4.72 m dims, 0.1% apart), COMBUSTOR SECTION dimension
diffuser_combustor.liner_source: estimate: liner annulus inside the measured case, dome just aft of the diffuser flange at s 3.093
diffuser_combustor.fuel_nozzles_note: not countable in the refs; estimate 24 (GE90 has 30 at a larger diameter, scaled by core size)

hpt.station_source: Airbus A380 AC PDF p.106, FIGURE-2-12-0-991-003-A01 Engine Dimensions - GP7200 (vector paths, 62.96 pt/m from the 4.93 m and 4.72 m dims, 0.1% apart), HP TURBINE dimension
hpt.counts_note: not found; modelling estimate NGV ~40-50, blades ~70-80 per stage
hpt.externals: ring of cooling-air / clearance-control manifolds and fittings around s 3.62-3.78 (p.106)
